subject: Security one-pagers: messaging review + do-not-say guidance (final pass this week)
body:
From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwoodinference.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Jan 27, 2026 at 9:12 AM PST
Subject: Security one-pagers: messaging review + do-not-say guidance (final pass this week)

Naomi — can you do a final messaging/accuracy pass on the 4 security one-pagers (SOC 2, ISO alignment, Data residency/retention, Encryption/KMS)? Goal is to lock copy this week so Design can finalize templates (DES-2911) and we can link these from the enablement kit index.

Key asks for your review:
1) Any technical inaccuracies or “too-strong” claims
2) Do-not-say / safe wording (especially ISO + pen test + “no training on customer data”)
3) Anything that implies roadmap / non-existent controls

Drafts folder (latest PDFs):
https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1Qm2Rk-SEC-KIT-onepagers-drafts

Attachments:
- Redwood_Security_OnePager_SOC2_v3.pdf
- Redwood_Security_OnePager_ISOAlignment_v2.pdf
- Redwood_Security_OnePager_DataResidency_v4.pdf
- Redwood_Security_OnePager_EncryptionKMS_v3.pdf
- Security_OnePagers_Signoff_Checklist_2026-01-27.docx

Stephanie — looping you in so Sales enablement can sanity-check that the language is “field usable” and doesn’t create procurement back-and-forth.

Thanks,
Camila

—
Camila Reyes
Product Marketing, Redwood Inference



From: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwoodinference.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Jan 27, 2026 at 11:03 AM PST
Subject: Re: Security one-pagers: messaging review + do-not-say guidance (final pass this week)

Reviewed all four. Overall: solid, close. Biggest risk is a few phrases that read like certifications or guarantees.

High-priority edits (please incorporate):

ISO one-pager
- Replace “ISO 27001 compliant” / “meets ISO 27001” with “security program is aligned with ISO 27001 control themes” (or similar). We should not imply certification.
- Add an explicit line: “Redwood is not currently ISO 27001 certified.”

SOC 2 one-pager
- Keep: “SOC 2 Type II report available under NDA upon request.”
- Avoid: naming the audit firm, opinion language, or stating “covers all products.” Use “Redwood’s hosted services” (and if Dedicated/Private are included, be explicit + accurate). If scope is unclear in the doc, keep it general and route evidence requests through GRC.

Data residency / retention one-pager
- The “EU data residency” section currently reads like we always process in-region. Please tighten to: residency is driven by deployment mode and selected region; Private deployments can be configured to keep data within customer-controlled environments.
- Avoid implying “customer controls log retention” for Hosted as a self-serve toggle unless we actually have it. It’s OK to say “available by request / contract” but don’t promise an on-console control.

Encryption/KMS one-pager
- Great overall. Only tweak: avoid “HSM supported” unless you mean via cloud KMS/HSM integrations in the customer’s environment (Private) or cloud-provider HSM-backed KMS (where applicable). Suggest: “supports integrations with cloud KMS; Private can integrate with customer-managed keys and, where applicable, HSM-backed key storage.”

Do-not-say guidance to include in the checklist (my suggestions):
- Don’t say “ISO certified” / “ISO compliant” unless GRC confirms.
- Don’t commit to pen test frequency (e.g., “annual”) unless we have a policy we are comfortable sharing. Use “regular independent penetration testing.”
- Don’t say “never retained” for prompts/outputs. Safer: “retention is limited and purpose-bound (e.g., abuse prevention/operations) and varies by deployment; details available in the retention overview.”

If you want, I can add markup in the docx checklist with exact replacement phrases.

Naomi

—
Naomi Feldman
Product Security PM, Redwood Inference



From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwoodinference.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Jan 27, 2026 at 12:18 PM PST
Subject: Re: Security one-pagers: messaging review + do-not-say guidance (final pass this week)

+1 to Naomi’s notes.

From the field side, two tweaks that will reduce churn:

1) “No training on customer data”
We keep getting trapped in “never uses data for anything” vs “training.” Recommend we add a single consistent sentence in each doc that touches data:
- “Redwood does not use customer prompts/outputs to train or improve general-purpose foundation models.”
Then point to the retention overview for ops logging details. Avoid absolute statements like “we never store.”

2) Data residency
AEs are already being asked “can you guarantee EU-only?” If the one-pager can explicitly say: “Hosted and Dedicated residency depends on selected region and service configuration; Redwood can support EU regions; Private/VPC can provide customer-controlled residency,” that’s super helpful.

If you want, I can also add a “What to say / what not to say” callout box at the bottom of each one-pager (but we should keep it short).

Stephanie

—
Stephanie Nguyen
Sales Readiness Lead, Redwood Inference



From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwoodinference.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Jan 27, 2026 at 2:46 PM PST
Subject: Re: Security one-pagers: messaging review + do-not-say guidance (final pass this week)

This is great, thanks both.

Plan:
- I’ll update copy tonight with the safe language (ISO alignment, pen test phrasing, residency nuance, “no training” line).
- I’ll also add a mini “Do / Don’t” footer on ISO + Residency only (not all four) to avoid clutter.

Naomi — yes please on the checklist markups. If you can drop exact wording in the docx (or reply inline), I’ll treat that as source-of-truth.

Also: do we want to explicitly mention “SOC 2 report under NDA” on ALL one-pagers or only SOC 2? I’m leaning only SOC 2 + a generic “evidence available under NDA” line elsewhere.

Camila



From: Aisha Rahman <aisha@redwoodinference.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwoodinference.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Jan 28, 2026 at 9:08 AM PST
Subject: Re: Security one-pagers: messaging review + do-not-say guidance (final pass this week)

Agree with Naomi/Stephanie.

Two additional guardrails (please keep these in the sign-off checklist):

1) Evidence gating
Don’t list specific artifacts (e.g., “full pen test report”) as generally available. Keep it: “available under NDA upon request” and route through the evidence request process.

2) Subprocessors / DPA
Avoid including any subprocessor claims in these one-pagers (they go stale quickly). We should point to the canonical subprocessor list / DPA process instead of embedding.

Re: whether to mention SOC 2 everywhere — use “compliance evidence is available under NDA upon request” in the non-SOC2 docs. Keep “SOC 2 Type II report…” only on the SOC 2 one-pager.

Once Camila incorporates edits, Naomi can do final technical check, then I’ll do a quick exec sign-off.

Aisha

—
Dr. Aisha Rahman
CISO, Redwood Inference



From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: Security one-pagers: messaging review + do-not-say guidance (final pass this week)

Updates made + re-uploaded as “v4” to the same folder.

What changed (high level):
- ISO: replaced “compliant” language with “aligned,” added “not currently ISO 27001 certified.”
- SOC 2: tightened scope language; left “Type II report under NDA” only here.
- Residency/retention: removed any “guarantee EU-only” phrasing; added deployment-mode caveat + pointed to retention overview.
- Encryption/KMS: clarified KMS/HSM wording to avoid implying a Redwood-managed HSM offering.
- Added a short “Do / Don’t say” footer to ISO + Residency only.
- Sign-off checklist updated with the do-not-say items + evidence gating + subprocessor/DPA note.

Folder:
https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1Qm2Rk-SEC-KIT-onepagers-drafts

Naomi — can you do a quick confirm that nothing regressed (esp. retention + audit log statements) and reply-all with “approved” when ready?
Aisha — once Naomi signs off, I’ll treat that as final and send to Design to lock templates.

Camila

—
Camila Reyes
Product Marketing, Redwood Inference
